source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"If source testing is negative, treat the injury as nonrecordable under OSHA Part 1904 because infection risk has been excluded.","B":"Record sharps injuries on the OSHA log when they cause lost work time or restricted duty, rather than when exposure alone occurs.","C":"For Part 1904-covered employers, record the contaminated needlestick and maintain required sharps information while protecting confidentiality.","D":"Keep the event in employee-health records but omit it from OSHA logs unless an occupational infection is later diagnosed."}}
source_row.rationale: OSHA requires work-related needlestick injuries from sharps contaminated with another person's blood or other potentially infectious material to be recorded when the employer is subject to Part 1904 recordkeeping. Such employers also maintain sharps-injury information while protecting employee confidentiality. Not every medical office is subject to the sharps-log requirement.
